document.title: Security Council resolution 2254 (2015)
document.source_note: Selected operative paragraphs 2, 4, 5 and 8. Whitespace-normalized English transcription; not the full resolution. Source paragraphs and existing repository assertion drafts remain available for human review.
document.rights_note: United Nations official resolution. Attribution retained; no institutional affiliation or endorsement.

spans.quote: 2. Requests the Secretary-General, through his good offices and the efforts of his Special Envoy for Syria, to convene representatives of the Syrian government and the opposition to engage in formal negotiations on a political transition process on an urgent basis, with a target of early January 2016 for the initiation of talks, pursuant to the Geneva Communiqué, consistent with the 14 November 2015 ISSG Statement, with a view to a lasting political settlement of the crisis;

4. Expresses its support, in this regard, for a Syrian-led political process that is facilitated by the United Nations and, within a target of six months, establishes credible, inclusive and non-sectarian governance and sets a schedule and process for drafting a new constitution, and further expresses its support for free and fair elections, pursuant to the new constitution, to be held within 18 months and administered under supervision of the United Nations, to the satisfaction of the governance and to the highest international standards of transparency and accountability, with all Syrians, including members of the diaspora, eligible to participate, as set forth in the 14 November 2015 ISSG Statement;

5. Acknowledges the close linkage between a ceasefire and a parallel political process, pursuant to the 2012 Geneva Communiqué, and that both initiatives should move ahead expeditiously, and in this regard expresses its support for a nationwide ceasefire in Syria, which the ISSG has committed to support and assist in implementing, to come into effect as soon as the representatives of the Syrian government and the opposition have begun initial steps towards a political transition under UN auspices, on the basis of the Geneva Communiqué, as set forth in the 14 November 2015 ISSG Statement, and to do so on an urgent basis;

8. Reiterates its call in resolution 2249 (2015) for Member States to prevent and suppress terrorist acts committed specifically by Islamic State in Iraq and the Levant (ISIL, also known as Da’esh), Al-Nusra Front (ANF), and all other individuals, groups, undertakings, and entities associated with Al Qaeda or ISIL, and other terrorist groups, as designated by the Security Council, and as may further be agreed by the ISSG and determined by the Security Council, pursuant to the Statement of the ISSG of 14 November 2015, and to eradicate the safe haven they have established over significant parts of Syria, and notes that the aforementioned ceasefire will not apply to offensive or defensive actions against these individuals, groups, undertakings and entities, as set forth in the 14 November 2015 ISSG Statement;

assertions.label: Convening negotiations
assertions.statement: In operative paragraph 2, the Council requests the Secretary-General, through his good offices and the efforts of his Special Envoy for Syria, to convene representatives for formal negotiations on political transition.

temporal_scope.source_target_expression: Target of early January 2016 for the initiation of talks; source wording retained without calculating a new deadline.

qualifications: The request is dated 18 December 2015. It does not establish that talks occurred or that particular representatives hold a present mandate.

assertions.label: A Syrian-led political process
assertions.statement: Operative paragraph 4 expresses support for a Syrian-led political process facilitated by the United Nations.
qualifications: This is the Council’s expressed support in the 2015 instrument, not a description of a current operating process.

assertions.label: Inclusive governance
assertions.statement: Within the process described in operative paragraph 4, the Council expresses support for establishing credible, inclusive and non-sectarian governance.

temporal_scope.source_target_expression: Within a target of six months, as stated in operative paragraph 4; no implementation date or outcome is inferred.

qualifications: This objective belongs to the process supported in the paragraph; no governance arrangement is asserted to have been established.

assertions.label: Constitutional drafting
assertions.statement: Within the same supported process, operative paragraph 4 envisages setting a schedule and process for drafting a new constitution.

temporal_scope.source_target_expression: Within a target of six months applies to the process language in the paragraph; no adopted timetable is asserted.

qualifications: The object is the proposed schedule and drafting process, not an adopted constitution.

assertions.label: Elections
assertions.statement: Operative paragraph 4 further expresses support for free and fair elections pursuant to a new constitution, under United Nations supervision, with participation including the diaspora.

temporal_scope.source_target_expression: To be held within 18 months, as stated in the source; no new deadline or current election date is calculated.

qualifications: The paragraph also specifies transparency and accountability standards.
Eligibility and supervision are objectives in the 2015 text, not statements of present electoral law or arrangements.

assertions.label: A condition-linked ceasefire
assertions.statement: Operative paragraph 5 expresses support for a nationwide ceasefire, linked in the text to initial steps by representatives toward a political transition under United Nations auspices.

temporal_scope.source_target_expression: To come into effect as soon as the described initial steps toward a political transition begin; this is a condition in the 2015 document.

qualifications: The source’s conditional linkage is retained. No ceasefire in force, current party commitment or present compliance is asserted.

ontology.title: Political research evidence model
ontology.status: Independent editorial ontology; no official UN endorsement

classes.label: Source Profile
classes.definition: A documented publishing identity and collection profile.
classes.scope_note: Keep existing source IDs. Do not automatically classify an outlet as a political actor.

classes.label: Document
classes.definition: A particular public source resource or version.
classes.scope_note: Keep canonical URL and existing document ID. In an RDF export, distinguish the source resource from its locally created receipt.

classes.label: Document Receipt
classes.definition: The locally created metadata record and collection history.
classes.scope_note: The receipt’s creation/retrieval time is not the publication time of the source document.

classes.label: Legal Instrument
classes.definition: A source-identified resolution, agreement or other instrument.
classes.scope_note: Instrument kind, issuer and symbol require source evidence. Legal force, amendment, entry into force and present applicability are separate assertions.

classes.label: Public Actor
classes.definition: A source-identified public institution, organization or professional public person.
classes.scope_note: Keep actor identity separate from publisher identity; do not instantiate private individuals. Offices, role holders and role dates require qualified assertions, not permanent inferred affiliations.

classes.label: Political Process
classes.definition: A documented process reference with explicit geographic and temporal scope.
classes.scope_note: Do not turn a document’s proposal into an actually operating process.

classes.label: Process Episode
classes.definition: A proposed, announced or reported meeting, consultation or negotiation episode.
classes.scope_note: Keep occurrence status, source date, event date and participant claims distinct.

classes.label: Normative Objective
classes.definition: An aim, requested action or proposed arrangement expressed by a document.
classes.scope_note: Use for the 2254 exemplar so governance, elections and ceasefire objectives do not become unqualified current-world facts.

classes.label: Assertion
classes.definition: An attributed statement or assessment, optionally with a subject/predicate/object structure.
classes.scope_note: Existing textual claims remain valid. Add structured triples only when the statement can be faithfully represented.

classes.label: Evidence Link
classes.definition: A document and locator tied to a particular assertion, with a stated evidence relationship.
classes.scope_note: Preserve existing document_id and locator; add supports_paraphrase / qualifies / contradicts / mentions, never an implied truth guarantee.

classes.label: Review Activity
classes.definition: A collection, annotation, extraction or review operation.
classes.scope_note: Record who or what performed it, its inputs and actual execution time. Do not invent a human reviewer.

classes.label: Review Decision
classes.definition: A versioned record of a review outcome and rationale.
classes.scope_note: Keep decision history; a current review label does not erase previous evidence.

classes.label: Concept
classes.definition: A controlled analytical term, distinct from a person, institution, place or event.
classes.scope_note: Use a shared scheme plus a Syria profile; multilingual labels are not entity-identity assertions.

classes.label: Place Reference
classes.definition: A named geographic scope, with optional existing navigation anchor.
classes.scope_note: Retain the current point basis and scope. A navigation point is not an incident geotag, political boundary or sovereignty claim.

classes.label: Institution or organization
classes.definition: A source-identified public institution or organization.
classes.scope_note: Roles and mandates require dated assertions.

classes.label: Public person
classes.definition: A public professional actor identified in a source.
classes.scope_note: Office, holder and role dates stay separate. No private-person profiles are supplied.

classes.label: Constituency reference
classes.definition: A constituency as described by a particular source.
classes.scope_note: A representation claim does not establish legitimacy, consent or exhaustive representation.

relations.label: published by
relations.meaning: The publishing entity of a source document. The legacy evidence graph uses the inverse source-to-document direction.

relations.label: supported by
relations.meaning: A qualified source relationship, not a bare claim of truth.

relations.label: requests
relations.meaning: The instrument explicitly requests an action; retain addressee and exact source verb.

relations.label: expresses support for
relations.meaning: Support expressed in the document; does not assert implementation.

relations.label: calls for
relations.meaning: Use only when this accurately represents the source wording; do not normalize every diplomatic verb to calls_for.

relations.label: has documented mandate
relations.meaning: Evidence describes a role/mandate, with the instrument and time scope retained.

relations.label: convenes
relations.meaning: Source reports actual convening; a request to convene belongs in requests instead.

relations.label: mediates
relations.meaning: A source describes a specific mediation role; distinguish the mandate, acceptance by parties and reported activity.

relations.label: invited to
relations.meaning: An evidenced invitation, not proof of attendance.

relations.label: participates in
relations.meaning: Participation is documented; role, date and source retained. Attendance does not establish representation of a population.

relations.label: consulted in
relations.meaning: The source describes consultation, separately from negotiation membership or decision-making authority.

relations.label: described as representing
relations.meaning: A particular source’s representation claim; no automatic claim of legitimacy, consent or exhaustive representation.

relations.label: explicitly references instrument
relations.meaning: An explicit document citation, not amendment, legal precedence or implementation.

relations.label: facilitates
relations.meaning: A documented facilitation role, distinct from mediation, convening or participation.
